subject.title: Invalid on-disk openclaw.json can brick managed gateway on next restart despite last-known-good

question: Should a managed gateway automatically restore a verified last-known-good configuration after invalid startup input, or should it remain fail-closed and only suppress restarts while the current valid process is still alive?
rationale: Both choices protect a real user need but trade channel availability against the risk of silently reverting intentional configuration. Existing recovery work explicitly distinguishes unsafe stale-snapshot cases, so source inspection alone cannot choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Adopt bounded managed recovery
options.body: Restore only a validated, policy-eligible last-known-good snapshot, preserve the rejected file for inspection, and notify the operator after channels return.

options.title: Keep startup fail-closed
options.body: Block restart when a live valid gateway rejects the disk snapshot, but require explicit Doctor or operator repair after a cold-start validation failure.

options.title: Defer to a broader rollback design
options.body: Fold this path into the canonical rollback proposal so startup, config writes, plugin validation, and update behavior share one documented policy.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded managed recovery
recommendation.body: Restore only a validated, policy-eligible last-known-good snapshot, preserve the rejected file for inspection, and notify the operator after channels return.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged recovery-policy work is the closest concrete ownership signal and already documents the stale-rollback boundary this decision must preserve.
